alt: A table comparing a bus and a bicycle. Cost per journey and time for a 5 km journey use like categories and are ticked. The reliability row is crossed because the bus is measured on reliability and the bicycle on fun.
caption: Every object must be measured on the same, relevant category.

alt: Two layouts. Point-by-point alternates A and B within each category (cost, time, safety). Block covers all of A, then all of B, in the same categories and order. Below, what each suits, its risk and a tip.
caption: Alternate for close comparison; use blocks for complex objects, keeping the categories in the same order.

alt: Douglass’s sentence sets one category, the effect of the nation’s freedom, against two objects: for “you”, his white audience, life and healing; for “me”, the enslaved, stripes and death. Parallel structure makes the two sides match.
caption: A single like category, in parallel grammar, makes the contrast sharp.

after: ## Worked example 1: building a comparison with like categories
alt: Paired bars compare a bus lane and a cycle track on three like categories using the lesson’s invented figures: cost per km (£2.0 million against £0.6 million), peak capacity (4,000 against 5,000 people an hour) and injuries a year (6 against 2). A commentary sentence turns the comparison into a claim.
caption: A comparison is evidence; commentary still has to say what it proves.

after: ## Worked example 2: describing what a comparison does in a text
alt: A flow: a letter and a text message share a feature (both carry news), differ on one category (the letter is edited in advance, the text afterwards), and the difference explains a conclusion about style: letters read like speeches, texts like conversations.
caption: Shared feature, one difference, one conclusion: the comparison explains style.

alt: A self-assessment grid with four criteria, category, like categories, organisation and claim, each described at three levels: not yet, getting there and secure.
caption: Secure comparisons name a relevant category, keep it like for like, and end on a claim.
